subject: Dedicated capacity uplift + autoscale policy during renewal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@olivetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft renewal: Dedicated uplift & scaling lifecycle proposal

Hi Priya —

Hope you're well. As OliveTech's renewal window approaches, I wanted to share a concise proposal for the Dedicated capacity uplift and the operational autoscaling changes we recommend during the new term. High level: you asked for predictable throughput and lower cold-start variance — the attached summary maps a commitment to 48 reserved GPUs with a small warm pool and tightened scale-up SLAs. Key bullets: 

- Committed capacity: 48 dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA H30-equivalent) across two regional pods for redundancy.
- Warm pool: 6 warm replicas (preloaded with the primary model) to reduce first-token tail latency during burst windows.
- Autoscale bounds: min_replicas = 6 (aligns with warm pool), nominal_replicas = 24, max_replicas = 60.
- Scale-up lag: target 60s cold-start SLO when warm pool exhausted; 95th percentile target.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline tokens/sec per-GPU and 99th-pct request latencies for your production routing (see attachment).
- Pricing: blended uplift rate (25% uplift on current committed spend) for the 12-month term, with a Q4 ramp credit to smooth first-month costs.

I've attached a short term summary and the operational runbook extract for the warm pool. If these numbers look sensible, Marissa and I can get the legal/contracting team to draft an amendment with explicit min/max replica definitions and the warm pool runbook attached.

Questions for you:
1) Do you prefer the warm pool capacity to be treated as part of the committed 48 GPUs or as an overlay burst credit?
2) Any blackout windows for autoscale during your nightly batch jobs?
3) Will procurement need a redline-ready term sheet or a summary first?

Thanks — can jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft renewal: Dedicated uplift & scaling lifecycle proposal

Sean —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications before we loop legal/procurement: 

- Warm pool treatment: Our finance/ops prefers warm pool included in the committed capacity (simpler for cost center allocation). Would that change the pricing math?
- Blackout windows: We have nightly model retrain pushes from 02:00–03:15 PT on Tuesdays; during that window we'd like autoscale to avoid scale-downs that could interfere with retraining I/O.
- Throughput guarantee question: Our SRE wants a 99th-percentile end-to-end latency target under your suggested nominal_replicas (24). Can you provide the historical percentile numbers for the last 30 days?

If you can answer these items, we'll prepare procurement and legal to receive the term sheet. Also include a proposed rollback/fallback plan in case initial weeks exceed expected token usage.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Desai
Head of ML Platforms, OliveTech
priya.desai@olivetech.com | +1 206-555-0277

Subject: Re: Draft renewal: Dedicated uplift & scaling lifecycle proposal

Thanks Priya — quick answers inline below and I attached the 30-day percentile extract and a short rollback playbook.

1) Warm pool as committed capacity: yes, we can include the 6 warm replicas inside the 48-GPU commitment. That will slightly increase the nominal_replicas math but keeps billing simpler. Updated breakdown in attachment: committed_reserve = 48, effective_nominal = 30 (24 active + 6 warm). Pricing impact: same uplift band but we shift how warm capacity is treated in unit economics — see page 2 of the summary.

2) Blackout windows: we can configure a schedule-driven autoscale hold during your retrain window (02:00–03:30 PT Tuesdays) to prevent scale-downs and I/O contention. We'll put that into the runbook and enforcement will be via scheduled policy on the Dedicated control plane.

3) 30-day percentiles: attached a lightweight extract (average token throughput and p50/p95/p99 latencies) for your production model under current commit. Short summary: under nominal load the p99 tail for first-token latency is ~1.2s; with warm replicas in place we project p99 down to ~250–350ms for the busiest bursts. These numbers assume our suggested warm pool and the 60s scale-up SLO if the warm pool is exhausted.

Rollback/fallback: included a three-step rollback plan in the runbook — 1) immediate autoscale cap to current committed capacity, 2) traffic shift to hosted fallback region for up to 30% of requests, 3) expedited support channel with one-hour response SLA for critical regressions.

I've attached: capacity_projection_q4.xlsx, 30d_percentile_extract.csv, warm_pool_runbook.md. Marissa/karthik — we'll need procurement/contract language: explicit definitions for min_replicas, nominal_replicas, max_replicas, warm_pool_count, scale_up_lag_seconds, and the throughput guarantee with measurement windows. Can you draft an amendment?

—Sean

Attachments: capacity_projection_q4.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB), 30d_percentile_extract.csv (csv, 23KB), warm_pool_runbook.md (md, 14KB)

Marissa/Sean —

Legal has a couple of standard asks before we route to procurement: 
- Can you provide a redline-ready term sheet (PDF + track changes Word) that contains the exact autoscale parameter definitions and the penalty/remedy language for throughput SLO misses?
- We also need data residency confirmation (all Dedicated GPUs in us-west2 region, no backups to other regions).

On the penalty language: OliveTech prefers a crediting approach for sustained misses (e.g., credits for each 24-hour window where p99 latency exceeds the committed target). Would Redwood be open to a capped credit schedule rather than financial termination?

If you can send the redline materials and a statement of data residency by EOD Monday, procurement will start processing the PO.

Thanks — Ben

Ben/Priya/procure —

Thanks for the quick turn here. Per the asks, attached is a redline-ready term summary (PDF) and a Word attachment with the autoscale parameter table you requested. Highlights/agreements agreed in this thread: 

- Committed reserve: 48 GPUs (includes 6 warm pool replicas).
- Autoscale parameters (explicit): min_replicas = 6; nominal_replicas = 30; max_replicas = 60; warm_pool_count = 6; scale_up_lag_seconds = 60.
- Throughput/SLO language: p99 first-token latency target = 350ms with measurement window = 30 days rolling; remedies = usage credit per 24-hr window where measured p99 > target (credit schedule attached; capped at 10% of monthly spend).
- Data residency: all Dedicated nodes will be provisioned in us-west2; backups and logs are also scoped to us-west2 unless otherwise requested.
- Term and pricing: 12-month term; uplift pricing as in OLV_Dedicated_Term_Summary_v2.pdf; PO instructions in DocuSign.

Next steps: 
1) OliveTech legal: please redline the Word term sheet and return to us.
2) Procurement: once redline is received we'll issue a final DocuSign link for signature and engage infra to schedule the capacity build (estimated 10 business days to provision).
3) Ops runbook handoff: we'll schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough with your SREs after signature.
